title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 162
paragraphs: During this Battus's reign things continued in this way, but in the reign of his son Arcesilaus there was great disturbance about the offices of the state. For Arcesilaus, son of Battus the Lame and of Pheretime, declared that he would not allow things to remain as Demonax of Mantineia had arranged them, and demanded back the royal rights of his forefathers. After this he stirred up strife, was defeated, and went into exile to Samos, while his mother went to Salamis in Cyprus. At that time the ruler of Salamis was Euelthon—the same man who dedicated as an offering at Delphi the censer well worth seeing, which is placed in the treasury of the Corinthians. Pheretime came to him and asked him for an army to restore herself and her son to Cyrene. But Euelthon was ready to give her anything else rather than that. When she received what he gave her, she would say that this too was a fine gift, but finer still would be that other gift—an army—which she kept asking for. As she kept saying this about every gift he gave, finally Euelthon sent her a present of a golden spindle and distaff, with wool on it. When Pheretime said the same thing about this present too, Euelthon replied that such things are given as gifts to women, not armies.
